edits.match: Annual influenza vaccine — universal adults ≥6 months; HD-IIV3, RIV3, or aIIV3 preferred
edits.new: **Annual influenza vaccine** — all persons ≥6 mo; HD-IIV3, RIV3, or aIIV3 preferred ≥65 yr (CDC; 2025–26 ACIP recs carried into 2026–27). AAFP additionally lists mRNA influenza vaccine (mFlusiva; FDA-approved Aug 2026, ≥50 yr) among preferred enhanced products ≥65; not in CDC preferential list.

edits.match: COVID-19 vaccine (2025–26 formulation) — per shared clinical decision-making
edits.new: **COVID-19 vaccine (2026–27 formulation)** — recommended for all adults ≥18 (CDC, 9/2026); ≥65 yr: second dose 6 mo after first (min interval 2 mo). Moderately / severely immunocompromised: per CDC clinical considerations.

edits.match: 2025–26 ACIP move to shared clinical decision-making is at odds with positions from ACP
edits.new: **COVID-19 vaccination.** The Sept 2025 ACIP vote moving COVID-19 vaccination to shared clinical decision-making, and all other post-6/11/2025 ACIP votes, were stayed by federal court order on 3/16/2026 (AAP v. Kennedy, D. Mass.; appeal pending, 1st Cir. No. 26-1503). CDC reverted to the July 2025 schedule and recommends the 2026–27 vaccine for all adults ≥18. AAFP (9/2026) concurs for adults ≥19, with a second dose ≥65; IDSA emphasizes immunocompromised adults. FLAG: federal recommendations may change again pending appeal or a reconstituted ACIP; recheck before each season.

edits.match: IDSA / ATS 2019 strongly recommends AGAINST procalcitonin to initiate antibiotics
edits.new: **2025 ATS update.** The 2025 ATS guideline (not IDSA-endorsed) readdressed only lung ultrasound (acceptable alternative to CXR / CT for diagnosis where trained operators are available; conditional, low quality), antibiotics in virus-positive CAP, duration (3–5 days non-severe once clinically stable; ≥5 days severe), and corticosteroids (against in non-severe; suggested in severe CAP). 2019 recommendations on follow-up imaging, cultures, urinary antigens, and procalcitonin were not revisited and remain the latest ATS / IDSA position. FLAG: ATS vs IDSA divergence on empiric antibiotics when a respiratory virus test is positive.

edits.match: Chest CT — for structural lung disease / bronchiectasis
edits.new: **Lung ultrasound** — acceptable alternative to CXR / CT for CAP diagnosis when performed by trained clinicians (ATS 2025, conditional). Does not replace selective 6–8 wk follow-up imaging.

edits.new: **Broad molecular profiling** — EGFR (incl. exon 19 del / L858R, exon 20 ins, uncommon S768I / L861Q / G719X), ALK, ROS1, BRAF V600E, KRAS (incl G12C), MET exon 14 skipping, RET, NTRK1/2/3, ERBB2 (HER2) mutation, NRG1 fusion; PD-L1 IHC — at diagnosis of advanced / metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC, before starting systemic therapy. Protein-overexpression IHC with therapeutic implications: HER2 IHC 3+ (fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan, subsequent line) and c-Met ≥50% IHC 3+ in EGFR wild-type (telisotuzumab vedotin). Repeat tissue / plasma ctDNA testing at progression (resistance mechanisms). Select squamous (never / light smokers, small biopsy).

Broad molecular profiling at diagnosis of advanced / metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, KRAS G12C, MET exon 14, RET, NTRK, ERBB2 / HER2 mutation, NRG1, PD-L1 IHC; HER2 and c-Met IHC overexpression); repeat at progression

edits.match: USPSTF and CMS cap at 80 and 77 respectively; NCCN Lung Cancer Screening
edits.new: **Upper age limit and eligibility for screening.** USPSTF (Grade B, 2021) and CMS NCD 210.14 cap at 80 and 77 respectively; both require quit ≤15 yr. FLAG: ACS (2023) screens current or former smokers 50–80 with ≥20 pack-years regardless of years since quitting; NCCN Lung Cancer Screening (v.1.2027) is broader still. Per synthesis rule, USPSTF / CMS criteria govern coverage and default eligibility.

edits.match: Serum calcium (corrected) — prior to each IV zoledronate or denosumab dose
edits.new: **Serum calcium (corrected) + Cr / eGFR** — before each IV zoledronate or denosumab dose. Denosumab in advanced CKD / dialysis (FDA boxed warning): assess for CKD-MBD before starting / continuing (nephrology input), correct hypocalcemia, supplement calcium + active vitamin D, and monitor serum Ca closely after each injection — highest risk weeks 2–10 (peak weeks 2–5).

Baseline secondary-causes labs (Ca, 25-OH vit D, PTH, alk phos, Cr / eGFR, Mg, TSH, CBC, 24-hr urine Ca) before anti-resorptive initiation; serum Ca + eGFR prior to IV zoledronate / denosumab dose; denosumab with advanced CKD / dialysis: serum Ca closely weeks 2–10 post-injection (FDA boxed warning); CTX / P1NP for adherence + response 3–6 mo after therapy start

edits.match: NCCN endorses routine CT every 6 months for 3 years in stage III-IV
edits.new: **Surveillance imaging in high-risk disease.** NCCN endorses routine CT every 6 months for 3 years in stage III-IV / serous / clear cell; ESMO and some SGO experts favor a more individualized, symptom-driven approach citing limited survival data. SGO's surveillance statement (Gynecol Oncol 2026) finds symptom review and physical exam the most effective recurrence-detection tools, vaginal cytology of negligible benefit, routine imaging without proven benefit outside specific settings, and ctDNA / novel serum biomarkers not yet ready for routine use.

edits.match: Serum CA-125 — only if elevated at baseline / diagnosis
edits.new: **ctDNA / MRD assays** — NOT recommended for routine surveillance outside trials (SGO 2026: requires additional study).

edits.match: For NMIBC, the AUA / SUO 2024 Amendment recommends
edits.new: For NMIBC, the AUA / SUO guideline (2016; amended 2020, 2024, 2026) recommends

edits.match: with no routine cytology or upper-tract imaging.
edits.new: with no routine cytology or upper-tract imaging. The 2026 amendment revised intermediate- and high-risk categories: all high-grade Ta tumors are now high risk (cystoscopy + cytology q3–4 mo × 2 yr, q6 mo yrs 3–4, then annually, with upper-tract imaging q1–2 yr); intermediate risk is now chiefly low-grade disease that is large, multifocal, or recurrent.

Urinary biomarkers — may be used to adjudicate equivocal cytology and to assess / predict response to intravesical therapy; do NOT replace cystoscopy; not routine in low-risk patients with normal cystoscopy

Urethral wash cytology periodically if urethra retained (especially with prostatic urethral involvement); normal cystoscopy + positive high-grade cytology → upper-tract evaluation, random bladder biopsies, prostatic urethral biopsies (blue-light cystoscopy when available); routine bladder cancer screening NOT recommended in asymptomatic adults (USPSTF I-statement)

edits.match: AUA / SUO has progressively de-escalated low-risk surveillance
edits.new: **Low-grade recurrence.** The 2026 AUA / SUO amendment permits active surveillance, in-office fulguration, or intravesical chemoablation for recurrent low-grade NMIBC (Conditional / Grade C) and for small papillary recurrence after low-grade Ta (Expert Opinion), in place of TUR under anesthesia.
